summary: Iteration 10 — Rota PDF export + Operations/Reports/Inventory/Workforce restructure + LocationSwitcher + non-Manager 'My Rota'. Backend: 5 NEW pytest cases for /shifts.pdf and /shifts?mine=true all green; full regression 180/180 passing. Frontend Manager flow verified end-to-end (Operations now only coupons+prep — old crashing tabs removed; Reports has labour widget + zreport/tippool collapsibles; Inventory has WastePanel under inv-toggle-waste; Workforce → Rota → rota-pdf-btn present; LocationSwitcher in header opens popover, lists loc_default, persists to kanda_pos_active_location_v1). Zero console errors during Manager navigation across all 5 screens. Cashier (PIN 2345) sidebar correctly omits Workforce/Staff/Operations and shows nav-my-rota; /workforce renders only wf-tab-myrota with myrota-empty card. Driver (PIN 4567) at /workforce works identically; HOWEVER on initial login Drivers are routed to /driver (DriverScreen) which has its own no-sidebar layout, so Drivers have no in-app way to reach /workforce. Backend cleanup performed: 18 leftover TEST QA staff + 3 leftover TEST_ customers from previous iterations deleted.

integration_issues.issue: LoginScreen.jsx line 41 redirects users with role=='Driver' to /driver (DriverScreen) which renders WITHOUT the POSLayout sidebar. nav-my-rota exists in POSLayout for non-Manager roles, but Drivers never see that layout from their normal login flow — they have no in-app link to /workforce. Manually navigating to /workforce works correctly (wf-tab-myrota + myrota-empty render fine). Either (a) add a 'My Rota' link inside DriverScreen header, or (b) route Drivers to / (POSLayout) by default and let them open the dispatch view from the sidebar.

integration_issues.flow: Cashier direct URL access to /operations and /staff
integration_issues.issue: Cashier can navigate to /operations and /staff via URL bar. The frontend route guard does not redirect — backend returns 403 for the data calls so the screens render in a broken/loading state and 6 axios 403 errors are logged to console. Not a security hole (data is gated) but a poor UX. Consider client-side role guard that redirects non-Managers off these routes.

action_items: Decide on Driver UX: drivers cannot reach /workforce from /driver. Either add a 'My Rota' button inside DriverScreen header, or route drivers to POSLayout root and surface their dispatch view as a sidebar entry.
Optional polish: add client-side role guard that redirects Cashiers/Drivers away from /operations and /staff to avoid the 6 axios 403 console errors and broken screens on direct URL access.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/shifts.py _render_rota_pdf: imports reportlab modules lazily inside the function — good for cold start. The PDF generation works correctly with proper Content-Disposition (attachment; filename="rota-YYYY-MM-DD.pdf"), media type application/pdf, body starts with %PDF magic. No issues.

POSLayout.jsx line 86: `staffUser && staffUser.role !== 'Manager'` correctly adds nav-my-rota for Cashier and Driver — but only renders when POSLayout is the active layout. Drivers land on /driver and skip POSLayout entirely.

All 5 of the previously-crashing useEffect(load, []) sites in OperationsScreen.jsx / StaffScreen.jsx are confirmed converted — no 'destroy is not a function' errors observed during navigation across Manager → Operations → Reports → Inventory → Workforce.

LocationSwitcher.jsx persists kanda_pos_active_location_v1 to localStorage on selection — verified. Cross-route data filtering by active location_id is correctly not implemented yet (per spec, future work).
Header at 1280×720 — Pay button overflow concern from iteration_9 not reproduced; document.scrollWidth == clientWidth (0px horizontal overflow) across Manager screens.

success_rate.frontend: Manager 100%; Cashier 100%; Driver 90% (My Rota works on /workforce; discoverability gap from /driver landing)

New iteration10 tests cover Rota PDF (Manager 200 + Cashier 403 + Driver 403) and /shifts?mine=true for Cashier+Driver. rca of the issue: Driver routing gap: /app/frontend/src/components/pos/LoginScreen.jsx line 41 — `navigate(user.role === 'Driver' ? '/driver' : '/');`. /driver renders DriverScreen which has its own minimal layout (just a header with name + Sign out + refresh, no sidebar). The new nav-my-rota link added to POSLayout for non-Managers is therefore unreachable for Drivers via normal navigation. Reproduction: login PIN 4567 → land on /driver → no sidebar/nav-my-rota visible. Mitigation: either add a 'My Rota' navigation entry inside DriverScreen, or change the login redirect so Drivers also use POSLayout.
